headline: CHINA COPPER IMPORT PREMIUMS HIT RECORD $500/T — Yangshan Surge Signals Beijing Sees Value As Spot Price Collapses
snippet: China's Yangshan copper import premium surged to a record $500 per tonne this week — the highest level ever recorded — before easing slightly to $495 on Friday, as Chinese buyers scramble to import copper even as LME prices tumbled into bear market territory at $12,235/t. The disconnect between China's physical buying urgency and the financial market selloff is the most important signal for junior copper investors this week: fundamental demand from Chinese manufacturers and infrastructure builders has not collapsed, even as leveraged positions unwind in London and New York. Tens of thousands of tonnes of US copper are now being routed to China in January deliveries, with sellers arbitraging the extreme Yangshan premium against falling US domestic prices. If the physical signal proves accurate, the financial market bearishness may be mis-pricing copper's near-term demand reality — a divergence that historically resolves through price recovery rather than demand destruction.

headline: PUREPOINT + ISOENERGY APPROVE 7,700M DORADO DRILL PROGRAM FOR 2027 — Q24 Target Advances After Summer Hole Hit 7.4m Elevated Radioactivity
snippet: Purepoint Uranium (TSXV: PTU) and partner IsoEnergy have approved a 14-hole, 7,700-metre diamond drilling program at the Dorado project in Saskatchewan's eastern Athabasca Basin, with Phase 1 beginning in January 2027 targeting the Q24 zone — where a summer 2026 discovery hole returned 7.4 metres of elevated radioactivity — and Phase 2 in July-August 2027 returning to the Nova zone, where earlier drilling reached 8.13% U₃O₈ over 0.4 metres. The 2026 season included 8,879 metres in 16 holes plus a 2,390-line-kilometre MobileMT survey. The Dorado JV's systematic step-out approach, funded through the program commitment, is designed to establish resource scale potential at one of the most closely watched emerging uranium targets in the Athabasca Basin — advancing while the uranium equity sector trades at a severe discount to spot.

headline: CHINA SMELTING AT CAPACITY CEILING — Price Drop Ignores Ore Shortage; Concentrate Processing Fees Turn Deeply Negative
snippet: China's copper smelting industry is hitting a structural ceiling, with the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association flagging this week that concentrate-fed smelting capacity has essentially run out of room to expand — a constraint that received almost no coverage during the financial market selloff. Combined with spot TC/RC processing fees falling into deeply negative territory (meaning smelters are paying miners for ore rather than charging for processing) and Chinese refined copper output declining 3% month-over-month in October, the ore shortage is creating supply tightness that runs directly counter to the bearish price narrative. SMM data places China's retail copper inventory at approximately 67,400 tonnes, a seasonal low. The analysis frames the copper bear market as primarily a paper-market phenomenon: forced liquidation by leveraged funds and momentum algorithms, while China's physical copper market continues to tighten.

headline: CERRADO GOLD EYES UPPER GUIDANCE AFTER Q3 OUTPUT CLIMBS 21% TO 16,685 GEO — Acquires Manantial Espejo Mine Post-Quarter
snippet: Cerrado Gold (TSXV: CERT) reported Q3 2026 gold equivalent production of 16,685 GEO at its Minera Don Nicolás mine in Argentina's Santa Cruz Province — up 21% year-over-year — driven by the selective routing of high-grade Calandrias ore to the Martinetas mill rather than the heap leach pad, with AISC of $1,546/oz. Year-to-date production reached 44,942 GEO, up 23%, and full-year 2026 output is now expected at the upper end of annual guidance of 50,000 to 60,000 GEO. Adjusted EBITDA was $33.8 million for the quarter and $90.8 million year-to-date. Post-quarter, the company completed the acquisition of Minera Tritón Argentina S.A., owner of the past-producing Manantial Espejo silver mine in Santa Cruz Province, adding a second Argentine asset with existing mine infrastructure as an organic growth platform. For junior gold investors watching the TSX-V selloff, Cerrado's strong operating results are a reminder that well-run producers are generating substantial free cash flow even at current, corrected gold prices.

headline: TSX VENTURE FALLS 3.71% ON WEEKLY CLOSE, SILVER SLUMPS 6.39% — Junior Mining Sector Absorbs Its Fifth Consecutive Weekly Loss
snippet: The TSX Venture Exchange closed the week down 3.71% as silver's 6.39% single-session decline on November 20 dragged the junior mining-heavy index sharply lower — the index's fifth consecutive weekly loss. The combined effect of gold's 14-month low, copper's bear market crossing, and silver's near-70% correction from its January all-time high has translated into severe bid-side withdrawal for most TSX-V mining companies, with mid-exploration-stage stocks bearing the brunt as retail capital retreats. For self-directed mining investors, the TSX-V's weekly close is a critical sentiment gauge: historically, sustained TSXV weakness beyond three consecutive months has preceded the capitulation lows that mark the major entry cycles for patient junior mining investors.

headline: GOLD WEEKLY FORECAST: HAWKISH FED AND AI DELEVERAGING CAST SHADOW OVER THANKSGIVING WEEK — Thin Liquidity Wednesday-Friday Could Amplify Any Surprise
snippet: FXStreet's weekly gold forecast for the Thanksgiving week identifies gold's break to 14-month lows near $3,500 as the dominant technical signal, with US bond and stock markets closed Thursday and an early Friday close creating thin institutional liquidity that could amplify any surprise economic data. The piece flags Fed Governor Waller's December hike commentary as the primary near-term headwind and identifies the December 1 PCE inflation print as the pivot point that will either accelerate the correction or begin a bottoming process. The analysis notes that any Fed pushback against consecutive rate hikes could trigger a sharp short-covering rally given the depth of current bearish positioning — but cautions that an oversold bounce and a durable bottom are very different market events, and that the first requires only a catalyst while the second requires a fundamental shift in the Fed narrative.

headline: STONEX: 'STRETCHED DOLLAR LEAVES GOLD AND SILVER IN NEED OF A REVERSAL' — New 2026 Lows With $3,837 Target If Bounce Materializes
snippet: StoneX's November 19 technical and macro analysis identifies gold and silver at their lowest 2026 levels, with the near-term forecast tilted downside despite increasingly oversold technical readings across both metals. Rising US yields and a hawkish Fed narrative are keeping the dollar at 2025 highs, maintaining maximum headwind against precious metals. For gold, StoneX identifies the $3,837-$3,870 band as the first significant resistance zone on any bounce — meaning a recovery from current levels of approximately $3,540 would need to clear roughly $300 of overhead resistance before changing the trend character. Silver's break below $45 is flagged as a further leg down in what has been one of the most dramatic 2026 corrections, with silver now trading more as an industrial commodity than a monetary metal in the current macro context. The analysis says a reversal signal requires a confirmed daily close above the first resistance band.

headline: COCHILCO: GLOBAL LITHIUM FLIPS FROM 79,000T DEFICIT IN 2026 TO 42,000T SURPLUS IN 2027 — Chile Output +3.1% To 335,000T
snippet: Chile's state copper commission Cochilco released its latest lithium market outlook on November 18, projecting a global lithium deficit of 79,000 tonnes in 2026 — driven by stronger-than-expected EV battery demand — flipping to a surplus of 42,000 tonnes in 2027 as new supply from Chile (+3.1% year-over-year to 335,000 tonnes), Argentina, and Africa comes online ahead of demand growth. Cochilco forecasts 2027 global demand at 2.25 million tonnes LCE (up 8% year-over-year) and an average lithium carbonate price near $18,500 per tonne — an upward revision from earlier 2026 forecasts that had priced in a faster, deeper surplus. For junior lithium investors, the 2026 deficit in Cochilco's data directly contradicts the narrative driving the current lithium equity selloff, suggesting financial markets are pricing in 2027's surplus before it arrives — a timing mismatch that has historically created entry opportunities in lithium equities.

headline: BRIXTON METALS CLOSES $1M FLOW-THROUGH FOR LANGIS SILVER-COBALT, ONTARIO — Insiders Fund Winter Drilling At Spot-Price Lows
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSXV: BBB) closed a C$1 million non-brokered private placement of national flow-through shares on November 20, with proceeds earmarked for exploration and drilling at its Langis silver-cobalt project in Ontario's historically productive Cobalt Camp. The timing — with silver trading near 14-month lows — is notable: sophisticated investors funding flow-through exploration at current silver prices are either making a macro contrarian bet or have high-conviction reasons tied to the specific asset's geology. Langis hosts historic silver and cobalt workings from early-20th-century mining alongside Brixton's modern exploration targeting open-pittable silver-cobalt-nickel mineralization — a structure that benefits from both silver price exposure and cobalt's strategic metal premium.

headline: GOLD BOUNCES 2.4% FROM 14-MONTH LOW AS DOLLAR SOFTENS — Mining Stocks Attract Bargain Hunters In Thin Pre-Holiday Session
snippet: Gold recovered approximately 2.4% from its 14-month low near $3,540 as a modest softening in the US Dollar Index attracted bargain-hunting interest in mining equities during thin pre-Thanksgiving trading, with producers and select TSX-V explorers attracting initial buying interest after weeks of relentless selling. The move does not reverse the broader correction — gold remains down approximately 25% from its November 5 near-term high and 36% from its January peak above $5,500 — but the intraday recovery pattern tracks prior oversold-driven technical bounces that have preceded each correction low in the current gold bull market. For mining equity investors, the question is whether the dollar softening that triggered the bounce reflects early positioning ahead of the December 1 PCE print, or is simply a one-day mean-reversion trade in thin Friday conditions.

headline: EMERITA RESOURCES $776M NPV SPANISH MINE PLAN ADVANCES — IBW Gold-Silver Project Submits Exploitation Licence, PFS Optimization Nears Completion
snippet: Analysis of Emerita Resources' (TSXV: EMO) flagship Iberian Belt West project in Spain highlights its progression toward mine development after completing bulk metallurgy testwork that confirmed improved economics: an after-tax NPV of US$776 million over a 21-year mine life, driven by gold and silver-bearing pyrite concentrate alongside zinc, lead, and copper production from one of Spain's largest undeveloped VMS deposits at 18.9 million indicated tonnes. The company has submitted all documentation required for a Spanish Exploitation (Mining) Licence, and the prefeasibility study optimization incorporating the revised two-stage flotation and post-flotation process — achieving 91.3% zinc, 85.8% copper, 80.5% silver, and 64.3% gold recoveries — is expected to be finalized in coming months. At current market capitalization, the US$776M NPV represents a substantial premium to Emerita's equity value, making it a name value investors in European gold and base metals may want to revisit as the correction matures.

headline: 'BEST TIME OF YEAR' FOR GOLD IS NOW — Sprott Money Sees Seasonal Window Opening For Precious Metals Recovery Into Year-End
snippet: Sprott Money's market commentary frames November's precious metals selloff against the strongest seasonal period of the year for gold and silver prices, arguing that the current correction has arrived at a historically favorable entry window that has often preceded sharp Q4 recoveries. The piece identifies a potential recovery above $4,100 gold and $54 silver as the technical signals that would confirm seasonal strength asserting itself over macro headwinds, while acknowledging that the Fed's hawkish stance represents the key obstacle to any seasonal pattern playing out. For self-directed mining investors building positions in junior explorers, the seasonal analysis points to Q4 as the period when junior gold companies traditionally attract speculative capital ahead of Q1 2027 financing windows — meaning a precious metals recovery, if it comes, would likely translate faster into TSX-V junior valuations than into large-cap producer prices.
